svg.title: Service, operator, SDK and contrib paths to staged RHOAI installer builds
svg.desc: SDK review, publication and dependency uptake join contrib review and adapter builds. Provider definitions and selected adapter references then join the service and operator synchronization, installer, bundle, catalog and stage gates. Dashed paths identify unverified handoffs.
svg.text: Four contribution paths → ODH images → RHOAI staged installer
As of 19 Oct 2026 · Current development · RHOAI release example: rhoai-3.6
Diamond = gate / selection Solid = verified configuration Dashed + ? = open handoff / enforcement
SEPARATE CONTRIB ENTRY PATH
Direct adapter / dependency / Containerfile / provider changes
start at the contrib PR below, independently of an SDK release.
SDK client / CLI-only updates:
Publish the package, install it and validate the target service.
An adapter or installer rebuild is not inherently required.
Adapter-facing SDK updates:
Update each consumer and rebuild its image before selection.
Package publication alone does not update adapter images.
SDK unit tests do not prove the adapter image SDK version.
Check the built image: requirements and constraints both apply.
P1 is conditional on provider-definition changes.
P2 applies to adapter selection, including image-only updates.
ODH DEVELOPMENT IMAGES / INSTALLER CONTEXT
RHOAI DEVELOPMENT → STAGED CATALOG
if provider definitions changed

g.title: Start with an SDK PR. Client/CLI-only consumers can stop after installing the published package; adapter-facing changes require a separate adapter image rebuild. The EvalHub Go service image does not install this Python SDK.
g.text: SDK change → upstream PR
eval-hub/eval-hub-sdk · models / client / adapter / CLI

g.title: Effective main rules require a PR and one approving review, with no required_status_checks rule returned. Classic branch-protection API returned 404. CODEOWNERS, last-push approval and thread resolution are not required by the observed rules. CI configures unit tests on Python 3.12/3.13/3.14, Ruff, mypy, pre-commit, commitlint and a Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL failure step. E2E has continue-on-error: true. Review and resolve applicable CI before merging as a working practice; these jobs are not established as enforced merge checks.
g.text: S1 · SDK review and configured CI
Effective main gate: PR + 1 approval; no required status checks
Unit Python 3.12–3.14, lint/type, pre-commit, commitlint, Trivy

g.title: main pushes build a dev distribution for TestPyPI. A published GitHub release triggers a separate build and upload to PyPI in the pypi environment using OIDC. Version comes from setuptools_scm and Git history/tags. Select the release/tag containing the merged change and verify the intended wheel/sdist is installable from the intended index. Neither publish workflow depends on the Tests workflow. Environment reviewer and tag/release authorization rules were not audited; TestPyPI success alone is not production publication.
g.text: S2 · Publish and verify the SDK package
main push → TestPyPI dev build; published release → PyPI
SCM-derived version; OIDC environments; approval policy? Q7

g.title: For adapter-facing changes, open a contrib PR for each affected adapter: update SDK requirements and any constraints/lock files together, migrate changed interfaces and exercise callbacks/results against the target service/sidecar. Inspect currently permits eval-hub-sdk[adapter]~=1.0.5 but its constraints pin eval-hub-sdk==1.0.5, and its Containerfile applies both. Regenerate constraints using the adapter README; do not assume a compatible range picks up a new release. Its unit workflow installs the SDK requirement without that constraints file, so verify the built image too. Direct SDK clients/CLI users instead install the published package and validate against their target service. No inspected workflow automatically opens consumer bump PRs or rebuilds adapters on SDK publication.
g.text: S3 · Update every affected SDK consumer
Contrib PR: requirements + constraints / lock + adapter migration
Verify installed SDK version; publishing alone does not rebuild

g.title: Direct adapter/framework/dependency/provider changes start here independently of an SDK release. Include main.py, Containerfile, requirements/constraints, tests and provider.yaml as applicable; new adapters also need the documented Makefile targets and README.
g.text: Contrib change → adapter PR
eval-hub/eval-hub-contrib · direct change OR SDK consumer bump

g.title: Effective main rules require a PR with one approval and allow squash merges only; no required_status_checks rule was returned, and classic branch-protection API returned 404. Run the applicable adapter-specific tests and inspect configured commitlint, CodeQL and Trivy jobs. Trivy has a HIGH/CRITICAL failure step. Provider validation runs for adapters/** PRs into main but its script only checks new adapter directories for provider.yaml existence and parseable YAML: it does not validate the full provider schema or existing directories. Test coverage is workflow/path-specific; a skipped job is not adapter validation.
g.text: C1 · Contrib review and configured CI
Effective main gate: 1 approval + squash; no required status checks
Path-specific tests; new-provider YAML; commitlint / security

g.title: After merge, build-images.yml detects changed adapters on main or v* branch pushes restricted to adapters/**; it is not a tag-push release trigger. It builds each selected Containerfile and pushes commit-SHA and channel tags (main → latest; otherwise branch name). A root-only/workflow-only change does not trigger this publisher, and SDK publication alone is not a contrib push. Manually dispatch with adapter input when change detection misses the needed rebuild; build-all-images.yml is a separate manual, explicit matrix, not dynamic discovery of every adapter. ToolEval expands to both adapter and toolbench-server images; clear maps to community-ibm-clear. RULER also has a separate publisher targeting the same tags. Quay credentials and a successful build/push are operational gates, but the publisher has no needs dependency on adapter tests or security jobs. The inspected workflow uses an Ubuntu docker build without an explicit multi-platform matrix. Verify digest, installed SDK/dependencies, architecture and runtime compatibility before selection.
g.text: C2 · Build and push the selected adapter images
adapters/** push to main or v* branch; manual rebuild available
quay.io/evalhub/community-<adapter>:<SHA> + latest / branch
Verify push, digest, actual SDK and supported architecture

g.title: If benchmark metadata, runtime fields or provider definitions change, reconcile the contrib provider.yaml into eval-hub/eval-hub config/providers/<id>.yaml in a separate PR and pass G1. The inspected contrib publisher does not copy provider definitions into EvalHub. EvalHub validates referenced images on matching PRs/pushes, but newly added providers are skipped on PRs and checked after merge. Its ConfigMap check runs on main pushes, nightly at 02:00 UTC and manual dispatch, not PRs; it detects drift against upstream TrustyAI and skips Kustomize image variables, so cannot prove the selected image digest. In a TrustyAI PR run hack/sync-evalhub-providers.sh <source-ref>, inspect generated ConfigMaps/kustomization and preserve intentional downstream overrides. For a new provider add the base Kustomize image variable and base/ODH/RHOAI params entries, then sync module manifests. Both service and operator PRs are conditional on the actual change.
g.text: P1 · Reconcile provider definitions when changed
Contrib provider.yaml → EvalHub config/providers PR (G1)
Image check skips new providers on PRs; drift check is post-merge
Sync operator ConfigMaps; update image variables / resources
Then join service and operator source promotion paths

g.title: For an adapter-only update, existing provider metadata may remain unchanged, but prove which reference and digest the deployment selects. TrustyAI base params uses community-inspect:latest while upstream ODH/RHOAI overlays and the inspected downstream rhoai-3.6 overlay select community-inspect:v0.6.12. A main/latest build does not update that pinned selection. Build the chosen release branch or deliberately change the selected reference in an operator PR; resolve and record its digest because channel/branch tags are mutable. Update affected params entries, run hack/sync-trustyai-module-manifests.sh to copy the config tree into trustyai-operator-module/config/manifests-template, review both trees, and pass G2 before G4/G6/G8 and G7/G9–G14 as applicable. The observed RHOAI overlay references a community adapter image, so do not assume a separate RHEL adapter rebuild/nudge. Confirm approved release/branch, platform/security eligibility and any mirror/rebuild/relatedImages mapping with maintainers (Q8).
g.text: P2 · Select adapter references and sync module manifests
Operator params.env: base, ODH and RHOAI overlays
Inspect: base latest; ODH / RHOAI v0.6.12 (not latest)
Copy generated config into module manifests; operator PR → G2
RHOAI branch mapping / rebuild or mirror / policy? Q8

g.title: Start with a PR in the canonical EvalHub repo. All binaries are built into the same container; the API, init, sidecar and MCP binaries do not represent four independent image promotion chains.
g.text: EvalHub PR → upstream main
eval-hub/eval-hub

g.title: This repository contains both the workload operator and the TrustyAI module operator. Follow both artifacts into the installer.
g.text: TrustyAI operator PR → upstream main
trustyai-explainability/trustyai-service-operator

g.title: Effective main rules require quality-checks, Gosec Security Scanner, gosec, dependency-review, CodeQL, docker-build-check; one review, code-owner review, last-push approval, stale-review dismissal and resolved threads. These are observed rules, not an audit of bypass actors. CI quality-checks runs formatting/vet, builds/tests including FVT, and documentation verification.
g.text: G1 · Required upstream merge gate
1 approval + CODEOWNERS + latest-push approval
Required checks + resolved review threads; up-to-date branch

g.title: GitHub workflows configure controller and module tests. Prow always runs images, and e2e runs for matching paths or an explicit test command. The enforcement layer was not established; do not infer that every listed workflow blocks merging.
g.text: G2 · Upstream CI / merge policy ? Q2
Controller + module smoke / manifest checks; Prow
Which checks and approvals are enforced remains open.

g.title: The hourly sync workflow uses a merge strategy, opens/updates a sync PR and fails on conflict. Effective main rules observed via GitHub require one approval. There is no workflow evidence that opening the sync PR automatically advances stable. Upstream CI also publishes quay.io/evalhub/evalhub independently.
g.text: G3 · Sync PR → ODH main
opendatahub-io/eval-hub
Hourly at :23 UTC / manual; conflicts fail; PR merge required

g.title: The workflow recognizes pull[bot], approves the sync PR and enables merge-commit auto-merge. This confirms the PR handling, but not the Pull app source configuration or sync schedule. Effective ODH main rules include one approval and CODEOWNERS/latest-push approval.
g.text: G4 · Upstream sync PR → ODH main
opendatahub-io/trustyai-service-operator
Pull bot PR: auto-approve / enable auto-merge; cadence ?

g.title: Sync main to stable is a PR workflow with fail-on-conflict=true. It must merge before the stable push image build runs. Required checks on stable were not established.
g.text: G5 · ODH main → stable sync PR
Push to main / manual creates sync PR
Gate: merge PR; resolve conflicts and destination requirements.

g.title: Two workflows open promotion PRs. Creating these PRs is not evidence they have merged. The module operator build currently targets main, while the workload operator stable definition targets stable.
g.text: G6 · ODH main → incubation → stable PRs
main push opens incubation PR; incubation push opens stable PR
Module image has a separate main build (Q3).

g.title: Stable EvalHub and TrustyAI workload PipelineRuns resolve odh-konflux-central pipeline/multi-arch-container-build.yaml. Module PipelineRuns target main and publish odh-trustyai-module-operator:odh-stable. Central scan task presence does not prove all findings block selection. Community quay.io/evalhub/evalhub is a parallel upstream output, not the RHOAI container being promoted.
g.text: ODH component image builds
EvalHub stable → quay.io/opendatahub/odh-eval-hub
Workload stable + module main → opendatahub operator images
Tag: odh-stable; Konflux build / scan tasks (policy: Q4–Q5)

g.title: Central rhods-devops-infra upstream-auto-merge runs at 0 */4 * * * UTC or manual dispatch. Its source map enables opendatahub-io/eval-hub main → red-hat-data-services/eval-hub main, preserving .tekton/* and global exclusions. The TrustyAI row instead points directly from trustyai-explainability main to Red Hat main and has automerge: no; it is excluded by the current scheduled selection. Merged PRs #437 (EvalHub) and #2036 (TrustyAI) corroborate those source branches and show manual sync PRs also occur. The separate main-release-auto-merge runs at 30 */4 * * * UTC; both component rows are enabled and releases.yaml currently lists rhoai-3.6. Its action resolves an unspecified source branch from the repository default, observed as main for both, then merges and pushes directly to the release branch. Main → stable is a separate daily 00:30 UTC PR/GAP path, not a configured prerequisite for main → rhoai-3.6. Q1 now concerns branch-policy enforcement, bypass permissions, conflict ownership and recovery rather than the source graph.
g.text: G7 · Central source sync into Red Hat release branches
EvalHub: ODH main → RH main; 4-hour automatic sync
TrustyAI: upstream main → RH main; auto off, manual PRs
Both: RH main → rhoai-3.6 every 4h :30; stable is parallel

g.title: ODH Update Manifest SHAs runs make update-refs-shas and resolves image digests when updates are needed, opening a PR. Failed component fetches add do-not-merge and fail the workflow. manifests-config.yaml pins TrustyAI module manifests from ODH main and keeps explicit image digests. Build Config separately lists selected relatedImages. These configurations can lag independently; atomicity was not established.
g.text: G8 · Select manifests + immutable image digests
Daily 06:00 UTC / manual manifest-update PR
Merge updated SHA / digest pins; eligibility policy ? Q4

g.title: The central release sync action merges the selected source and pushes directly to the release branch; it does not create a release PR. Successful pushes still depend on credentials and destination branch policy. Non-excluded merge conflicts fail the action; excluded files are restored from the destination. Manual PR/backport paths also exist. The inspected gatekeeper calls shared post-codefreeze logic for two EA branches; confirm effective required checks, bot bypass permissions and branch coverage rather than assuming every development update passes a release PR or an EA gate.
g.text: G9 · Accept a release update / backport
Central sync merges/pushes directly; conflicts and branch policy apply
Manual sync / cherry-pick PRs are additional paths
EA gatekeeper coverage / effective bypass policy remain open

g.title: The checked-in CI push pipeline builds Dockerfiles/rhoai.Dockerfile with BUILD_TYPE=CI via multi-arch-operator-build.yaml and nudges bundle/bundle-patch.yaml. A component image existing in Quay does not itself update this source build.
g.text: ODH installer operator build
opendatahub-io/opendatahub-operator main push
Output: opendatahub-operator:odh-stable; path filters apply

g.title: Verified release PipelineRuns build source/images from downstream Dockerfile.konflux definitions for x86_64, ppc64le, s390x and arm64. Each inspected component push pipeline sets build-nudge-files to build/operator-nudging.yaml. Image publication and policy approval are separate states.
g.text: RHOAI component image builds
Release-branch push → Konflux hermetic builds
EvalHub + workload + module → quay.io/rhoai/*-rhel9
Four architectures; scans / attestations policy ? Q5

g.title: The ODH bundle CI PipelineRun publishes opendatahub-operator-bundle:odh-stable and nudges catalog/catalog-patch.yaml. A bundle-patch-only change is excluded from the direct bundle build and needs processed output. Bundle Sync CI generates bundle content from opendatahub-operator stable. The complete active ODH processor/catalog policy was not audited; this is contextual to the requested ODH image endpoint.
g.text: ODH development bundle / catalog path
ODH-Build-Config pins relatedImages; bundle build
Operator stable → bundle sync every 2h / manual
Bundle → catalog nudge; processor / policy details ? Q4–Q5

g.title: The installer insta-merge workflow restricts handling to konflux-internal-p02[bot], permitted title/version pattern and exactly the nudging file. It invokes shared insta-merge logic; this file alone does not establish additional CI or policy verdicts required before the nudge is emitted. The Operator Processor runs on an eligible bot push or manual dispatch.
g.text: G10 · Component digest nudge PR → installer
rhods-operator build/operator-nudging.yaml
Bot + one-file + title/version feasibility → auto-merge path

g.title: The processor combines Build Config relatedImages with nudged digests, resolves image git.url/git.commit labels for manifest entries, and commits generated operands and prefetched content. A qualifying release-branch push builds the installer and nudges RHOAI Build Config bundle/bundle-patch.yaml. The nightly workflow is workflow_dispatch; its external cadence was not established.
g.text: G11 · Assemble + build RHOAI installer operator
Processor: digests → operands map + source manifest metadata
Prefetch matching manifests; publish odh-rhel9-operator
Nightly/manual refresh is a separate route.

g.title: RHOAI Build Config bundle-insta-merge validates bot and changed-file feasibility. Process Operator Bundle handles the input change and commits processed bundle/Helm content. The generated content, not merely a bundle-patch edit, triggers the bundle build. Helm builds are parallel outputs; this diagram follows OLM bundle/catalog to the staged installation endpoint.
g.text: G12 · Operator nudge → processed bundle / Helm
Bot / file / title checks → bundle nudge merge
Process CSV + relatedImages / Helm values, then build
bundle-patch-only push is excluded from direct Tekton build.

g.title: The bundle build nudges catalog/catalog-patch.yaml. Process FBC Fragment refreshes PCC, selects snapshot bundle images and commits catalog content. The direct FBC push trigger excludes catalog-patch-only changes. The inspected IntegrationTestScenario still names the 2.17 application and cannot establish the live 3.6 EC gate.
g.text: G13 · Bundle digest → catalog processing → FBC build
catalog/catalog-patch.yaml nudge; process catalog content
Refresh PCC + select bundle snapshot; build FBC fragment
Policy / integration-test enforcement remains Q5.

g.title: Push To Stage accepts an FBC image (or LATEST_NIGHTLY), checks signed-image presence, validates/regenerates PCC, patches the stage catalog on Build Config main and monitors resulting catalog builds. A signature-presence check is not evidence of a full Enterprise Contract verdict. Required QE sign-off and the external trigger are not established.
g.text: G14 · Promote selected FBC to stage ? Q5–Q6
Push To Stage: workflow_dispatch; select FBC / latest nightly
Validate signed-image presence + catalog/PCC data
QE sign-off, release-policy binding and caller / cadence: OPEN

g.title: Endpoint requested by the user. Record the catalog digest, bundle digest, installer digest and related component digests together to trace which upstream commit is actually installable. Successful workflows alone do not prove the cluster installs the intended image set.
g.text: QE-installable staged catalog
Built stage catalog → OLM bundle → installer / module / workloads

svg.text: OPEN QUESTIONS TO CLOSE
Q1 · Which source-sync controls and recovery rules remain unverified?
Component maintainers / DevOps
Q2 · Which TrustyAI tests actually block merges?
Repository / CI owners
Q3 · Are module and workload images intentionally built from different branches?
TrustyAI / ODH maintainers
Q4 · What makes an image set eligible for installer selection?
Build / integration owners
Q5 · Which QE / Enterprise Contract verdicts are mandatory?
QE / Konflux / release engineering
Q6 · Who triggers and approves promotion to the staged catalog?
Release engineering / QE
Q7 · Who authorizes SDK releases and consumer uptake?
SDK / adapter maintainers
Q8 · Which adapter image is approved and installed?
Adapter / operator maintainers / QE
Detailed gate criteria and pinned source links: evidence.json / companion guide.
SDK/contrib rules require approval; configured CI is not automatically a merge requirement.
Verify installed adapter digest and SDK version alongside installer / catalog provenance.
Source links are embedded in nodes. No release, build or promotion was triggered during this research.
